strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and flick up to the right
lift, draw the upper bar from left to right
lift, draw the lower bar from left to right
lift, begin at the upper bar and draw the vertical down through the lower one, then without lifting loop round to the left and back up, cross the vertical and run out to the lower right
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 0307c file records ぼ as six stroke paths in this order and direction: ほ's four strokes (the left vertical with its flick, the upper bar, the lower bar and the vertical with its loop), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are five pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/0307c.svg, hiragana ぼ (U+307C HIRAGANA LETTER BO), six stroke paths kvg:0307c-s1 to s6 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s4 are ほ's strokes, the same paths as in its file for ほ, kanji/0307b.svg; s5 and s6 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. KanjiVG's left vertical ends in a flick up to the right, as in its file for ほ, kanji/0307b.svg, and as in は. This inventory's ほ row, which cites Sirgazil's animation, says that stroke hooks left at its foot; this path follows KanjiVG, and, as in は, goes down to the foot of the print stroke and climbs back a short way before the flick. KanjiVG's last stroke starts at the upper bar, not above it, and so does the print glyph's.

notes: ほ voiced. The three of さんぼん, where the counter for long thin things takes the mark the reader has had since chapter three.
